title: Human intestinal microbiome determines individualized inflammatory response to dietary emulsifier carboxymethylcellulose consumption
authors: Daniel N, Wu GD, Walters W, Compher C, Ni J, Delaroque C, et al.
journal: Cellular and Molecular Gastroenterology and Hepatology
population: Germ-free Il10-deficient mice colonised with faecal microbiota of 2 carboxymethylcellulose-sensitive and 2 insensitive participants of the 2022 feeding trial; 3 to 4 mice per group
funder: European Research Council Starting Grant ERC-2018-StG-804135; IdEx Université de Paris (ANR-18-IDEX-0001); Fondation de l'Avenir (AP-RM-21-032); Agence Nationale de la Recherche grants ANR-21-CE15-0042-01 and ANR-20-PAMR-0002; INSERM programme Microbiote; National Institutes of Health grants DK115180, 5UL1TR001878 and P30-DK050306; Penn Center for Nutritional Science and Medicine; Max Planck Society.
result: After 16 weeks of carboxymethylcellulose, mice colonised with microbiota from either sensitive donor showed shorter colons, larger spleens, higher histological inflammation scores and microbiota encroachment; mice colonised from insensitive donors did not. Sensitive participants carried no NOD2 mutations, and ATG16L1 variants were distributed regardless of sensitivity.
